title: Virgo Cluster Excerpt: NGC 4261
caption: The elliptical galaxy NGC 4261 and neighbors, imaged by the NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory
celestial: NGC 4261 · constellation Virgo · about 100 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A trail of galaxies and stars runs through this small section of one of the First Look images from the NSF–DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory. Dominating the upper half is NGC 4261, a large elliptical galaxy, while the lenticular galaxy NGC 4281 sits at the bottom left.

Between and around them lies a crowd of other galaxies and stars. NGC 4261 is about 100 million light-years away, in the direction of Virgo. Elliptical galaxies are smooth, rounded collections of stars with little gas and few newly forming stars, while lenticular galaxies have a disk like a spiral but lack prominent spiral arms.

The view was captured with the LSST Camera on Rubin's Simonyi Survey Telescope, combining exposures through u, g, r and i filters. Stacking many exposures lets faint galaxies emerge that a single short look would miss, helping to bring out the many objects between and around the two big galaxies.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (45.32 x 45.32 arcminutes) and distance (100 million light years), the frame spans roughly 1.3 million × 1.3 million light-years. Its light set out about 100 million years before reaching the telescope.
